description: Password hashing + KDFs decomposed. Why generic hash isn't enough (rainbow tables, brute force). Salt + pepper. PBKDF2 → bcrypt → scrypt → Argon2 evolution. Memory-hard vs computation-hard. Cost calibration. HKDF for symmetric key derivation.

sub_mechanisms.name: rainbow_table_attack
sub_mechanisms.definition: Precomputed table: hash → password. Lookup compromised hash to recover password.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bare SHA-256 of password trivially reversed. Mitigation: salt makes precomputation impractical. Foundation of password-storage best practice.

sub_mechanisms.name: salt_per_user
sub_mechanisms.definition: Random value unique per password. Stored alongside hash. Hash(salt + password).
sub_mechanisms.why: Eliminates rainbow tables. Each salt requires its own precomputation. Standard practice. Don't reuse salts across users.

sub_mechanisms.name: pepper_application_secret
sub_mechanisms.definition: Application-wide secret added to password hashing. Not stored in database.
sub_mechanisms.why: Database compromise doesn't give attacker the pepper (lives in app code/HSM). Additional defense layer. Recovery if pepper changes is challenge.

sub_mechanisms.name: PBKDF2_iteration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Apply HMAC iteratively (~100K-1M times). Cost scales linearly.
sub_mechanisms.why: First widespread password KDF. RFC 8018. NIST-approved. Not memory-hard: GPU/ASIC accelerate dramatically. Modern: Argon2 preferred.

sub_mechanisms.name: bcrypt_blowfish
sub_mechanisms.definition: Based on Blowfish cipher. Memory-hard (4 KB). Adaptive cost factor.
sub_mechanisms.why: Long-standing default. Bounded password length (72 bytes) quirk. Cost factor (2^N rounds) increases over time. Still solid choice.

sub_mechanisms.name: scrypt_memory_cost
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory-hard function. Cost = N (CPU) × r (block) × p (parallel).
sub_mechanisms.why: Designed to defeat ASIC. Variable memory (typically 16-128 MB). Pre-Argon2 default. Litecoin's proof-of-work foundation.

sub_mechanisms.name: Argon2id_recommended
sub_mechanisms.definition: Hybrid Argon2: combines i (side-channel resistant) + d (GPU resistant) variants.
sub_mechanisms.why: OWASP recommended. Memory-hard, configurable. Argon2 won Password Hashing Competition 2015. Standard for new applications.

sub_mechanisms.name: cost_calibration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Choose KDF parameters so hashing takes ~100-500ms on server. Slow enough to deter brute force.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tradeoff: longer = more secure but UX impact + DoS risk. Calibrate to server capacity. Modern: ~300ms common. Increase as hardware advances.

sub_mechanisms.name: memory_hard_GPU_resistant
sub_mechanisms.definition: Forces attacker to use slow GPU/ASIC memory. Memory ~10x more expensive than computation on parallel HW.
sub_mechanisms.why: PBKDF2's CPU cost trivially parallelised (GPUs). Memory-hard equalises: 1024 GPU cores need 1024× memory. Forces attacker to slow primary memory.

sub_mechanisms.name: HKDF_key_derivation
sub_mechanisms.definition: HMAC-based KDF. Extract-then-expand: extract entropy from secret, expand to multiple keys.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard KDF for symmetric keys (not passwords). Used in TLS 1.3, Signal. Different from password KDFs — no need to be slow.

sub_mechanisms.name: argon2_parameters
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory (m), iterations (t), parallelism (p). OWASP: m=46 MB, t=1, p=1 (recommended baseline).
sub_mechanisms.why: Tune to your workload. Higher memory = more GPU-resistant. Higher iterations = more CPU cost. Storage of params with hash needed for rehashing.

sub_mechanisms.name: password_rehashing_on_login
sub_mechanisms.definition: On successful login, check if hash uses outdated params. If so, rehash with current params.
sub_mechanisms.why: Migrates users to stronger params over time. Without it, hash-cost-factor stuck at original setting. Standard pattern for KDF parameter evolution.

derivation_rules.name: salt_eliminates_rainbow_tables
if: each password is hashed with unique salt
derivation_rules.why: Salt is the input variation. Attacker must compute table per salt = impractical at scale. Every modern password storage uses salt.

derivation_rules.name: memory_hard_KDFs_neutralise_GPU_attack
if: KDF requires significant memory per attempt
derivation_rules.why: GPUs cheap per core but memory bandwidth limited. Memory-hard: each parallel attempt needs its own memory. Bandwidth becomes bottleneck. Argon2/scrypt key insight.

derivation_rules.name: cost_calibration_per_server_capability
if: server is calibrated to ~300ms per hash
then: attacker faces same cost per guess
derivation_rules.why: Linear cost per guess. Strong passwords + slow KDF = brute force impractical. Trade-off: too slow = user wait + server load + DoS risk.

derivation_rules.name: Argon2id_modern_default
derivation_rules.why: Memory-hard + side-channel + GPU resistant. Won Password Hashing Competition. Solid choice. bcrypt still acceptable for legacy/embedded.

derivation_rules.name: rehashing_pattern_migrates_users
if: login flow rehashes with current params on success
then: users gradually migrate to stronger settings
derivation_rules.why: Increase params, mark old hashes for rehash. Active users update on next login. After ~6 months, most active accounts on new params. Standard upgrade pattern.
